task_name: The checkout's specs, read and written from disk

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each has production lines behind it. (a) 'finds the newest execution spec of a checkout, reads it': DiskEpicSpecs#mostRecent joins root.text with DIRECTORY, lists it, filters by SUFFIX in #newestOf and takes matching.sort().at(-1), then reads that absolute path in #textOf and builds EpicSpec with the path relative to the checkout root, exactly as the task's 'path is relative to the checkout root' sentence asks. (b) 'writes it back': rewrite({root, spec, text}) joins root.text with spec.path and calls the injected write with that absolute path and the new text. (c) 'telling a disk that refused apart from a file that is no spec': a list or a read that throws, and a listed file whose read answers null, become EpicSpecNotRead, while a file whose EpicSpec#title() is null becomes EpicSpecNotUnderstood; both leaves plus EpicSpecNotWritten reach the wire as distinct codes in PlanCollapse. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line names it('answers the newest execution spec and leaves the design documents and the template out') and fixes its input and its assertion. The test in the diff is that test: list answers the four names the plan wrote, in the plan's order ('_TEMPLATE-execution-spec.md', '2026-09-01-a-execution.md', '2026-09-11-b-design.md', '2026-09-11-b-execution.md'), and the assertion is expect(read).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/repo/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11-b-execution.md') — the same input, the same expected value, and the two dated executions present so the older one has to lose. It adds one assertion beyond the plan's sentence (the returned EpicSpec equals one built with the relative path and the text read), which is the same behaviour pinned tighter, not a different assertion.

Compared name by name. Port: 'export class EpicSpecs' with 'async mostRecent(root: CheckoutRoot): Promise<EpicSpec | null>' and 'async rewrite({ root, spec, text }: { root: CheckoutRoot, spec: EpicSpec, text: string }): Promise<void>' — parameter names, order, destructured shape and return types are the brief's, and the bodies throw the 'must implement' sentence of the named exemplar backend/src/domain/ports/pull-requests.ts. Adapter: 'export class DiskEpicSpecs extends EpicSpecs', 'static readonly DIRECTORY = 'docs/superpowers/specs'', 'static readonly SUFFIX = '-execution.md'', constructor({ list, read, write }) with the three function types the brief spells (list -> Promise<string[] | null>, read -> Promise<string | null>, write(path, text) -> Promise<void>). Exceptions: the four classes with the exact inheritance the brief states (SpecFreezeFailure extends PlanFailure; the three leaves extend SpecFreezeFailure). Wiring: the three PlanCollapse entries carry the literal codes 'epic-spec-not-read', 'epic-spec-not-understood' and 'epic-spec-not-written', and plan-refusal.test.ts's FAMILIES gains 'SpecFreezeFailure'. The two behaviours stated in prose also hold: list answering null returns null and is no failure, and the title()-is-null refusal is EpicSpecNotUnderstood.

Row by row against the diff. D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript): both new modules and the new test are .ts, with relative imports naming the .ts extension. D-11 (a yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented): the adapter grows no opinion of its own about whether a spec is freezable — it asks EpicSpec#title(), and EpicSpec is the value that already imports analyzeSpecFreeze from plugin/scripts/groom.js. D-13 (no phase is stored): mostRecent derives everything from what the checkout holds and writes no state. D-22/D-23/D-7 speak about the gate, the push and the merge, which this task does not reach; D-1, D-6, D-16, D-18, D-21 and D-25 have no subject in a port, a disk adapter and three refusal codes. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: the port is the pull-requests.ts idiom verbatim (throwing 'must implement <method>(...), asked for ...'), and the adapter is disk-conversation-records.ts's idiom — same ReadText/WriteText local types, same injected read/write held as readonly fields, same super() then assignment, same 'could not be written: ${String(cause)}' translation of a disk error into a typed domain failure. The new test mirrors disk-conversation-records.test.ts (module-level real value objects, vi.fn() doubles for the injected functions, rejects.toBeInstanceOf for each leaf). backend/conventions/this-repository.md: the exception family names its two causes as that document requires (*NotRead/*NotWritten for the command failing, *NotUnderstood for an answer we cannot read), the four exceptions join the one catalogue exceptions.ts, the port lives in domain/ports and the adapter in infrastructure, and each code is kebab-case and declared explicitly beside its cause rather than derived from the class name (conventions/boundaries.md: 'The code of an answer is declared explicitly, beside its detail, and never derived from an exception's class name'). CLAUDE.md's language rule: every identifier, test name and diagnostic in the diff is English. conventions/architecture.md: domain imports only domain, infrastructure imports domain, one concept per module. conventions/testing.md rule 2: the adapter is cut right before the external system and both failure causes are told apart with the not-instance-of assertions the document asks for; the declared shapes are real (docs/superpowers/specs holds 2026-09-11-...-execution.md and -design.md today, and plugin/templates/_TEMPLATE-execution-spec.md exists), and the plan's own task text is where that provenance is written. conventions/defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — no classifying value is held as a loose string or boolean and there is no dispatch with a catch-all; the failure vocabulary is the three exception types and the PlanCollapse map raises for anything undeclared. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: mostRecent returns EpicSpec | null and rewrite returns void; nothing hands a map to a consumer that decides with it. (3) two fields that have to agree, sentinels included — no subject: the adapter holds no flag beside a value, and no empty string or zero stands for an absence; absence travels in the type. (4) errors named for what happens — conforme: EpicSpecNotRead, EpicSpecNotUnderstood and EpicSpecNotWritten name what happened to the spec, not the module that raised it, and each inherits from the family that fits rather than from the root. Three tensions considered and deliberately left out of the findings: the 'EpicSpec | null' absence (defects.md would prefer a member of a vocabulary, but the plan closed that return type literally in its Contract block and it is the host idiom of recall()/openOf(), so the objection is with the plan, not the diff); the absence of a cap on the disk calls (boundaries.md asks for one, and the constructor's shape is closed by the same Contract block); and the port's 'spec?.path' in a message where spec is typed non-nullable, which is copied from the exemplar the plan named. Delivery shape: no document of either yardstick prescribes one for adding a port and its adapter, and the diff breaks no call site — the three PlanCollapse entries are additions to an existing frozen map.

The diff has exactly one '-' line in a test file: the FAMILIES array of plan-refusal.test.ts, rewritten to append 'SpecFreezeFailure'. No assertion, case or test is removed, and the rewrite is asked for by the task's own text ('that test's FAMILIES gains SpecFreezeFailure'), which is what keeps the family — as opposed to its three leaves — out of the set required to carry a refusal, the same treatment the other fifteen families already get. The three leaves are simultaneously added to PlanCollapse, so the test's demand of one refusal per leaf stays as strict as it was.

The promised behaviour lives in production code. Newest-wins is DiskEpicSpecs.#newestOf (filter by SUFFIX, sort, take the last), the relative path is built in mostRecent, the write path in rewrite, and the three failures in #listed, #textOf and the title() check. The test's scaffolding is only the injected list/read/write doubles — the seam the plan's own constructor contract defines — and the expected values it asserts (the absolute path read, the EpicSpec returned, the write arguments, the exception types) all come back from the adapter. Revert disk-epic-specs.ts and every one of the five tests fails at import.

The diff writes only what the task asks inside its six declared files: two new modules, four exception classes appended to the catalogue, one import line and three map entries in start-plan-route.ts, one array element in plan-refusal.test.ts and the five tests the Tests line names. No refactor, no rename, no adjacent fix, and nothing the task did not ask for was added to start-plan-route.ts or exceptions.ts. The out-of-scope list is untouched: no plugin script, no skill, no route of start-plan/implement-plan behaviour, no groom, no merge or pull-request write. There is no hunk of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-issue-329-gate-1-the-freeze.md in the diff, so no amendment was made — I compared the plan's Task 2 section in the repository with the brief and they are identical, verification commands and Tests list included.

Five new tests, all in disk-epic-specs.test.ts. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no filesystem and no randomness — every input is an injected vi.fn() and the only shared values are frozen value objects and string constants. Isolated: each test constructs its own DiskEpicSpecs with fresh doubles, nothing mutates shared state and no test depends on the order of the file; the third one runs its two adapters through Promise.all but they share nothing. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on what the adapter did at its boundary — the absolute path read, the EpicSpec returned, the (path, text) pair written and the exception type raised — which is what conventions/testing.md's adapter row asks for, not a mock's call count standing in for behaviour. I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and found nothing in it or in its testing-anti-patterns reference that these tests contradict: the doubles are the adapter's designed injection seam rather than mocks of the code under test, each name is a sentence about what is guaranteed, and no test-only method was added to production code.
